declarations.description:
Shows a menu where its content is right-clicked, long-pressed on a touch screen, or asked for with the keyboard's
context-menu key or Shift+F10. Wrap the area in `c2-context-menu`: only its default-slot children open the menu,
never the menu itself. The element adds no box of its own (`display: contents`), so it can wrap a table cell grid,
a canvas or a whole panel without changing the layout.

The menu is a `c2-menu` positioned at the pointer, with its keyboard support, submenus and checkable rows. Give it
either way, or both:

- **Static:** a `c2-menu` slotted into `menu`, the same menu wherever the area is clicked (zoom in, zoom out, reset).
- **Dynamic:** a `renderContextMenu` function, called on every opening with the ContextMenuContext, which
  returns the rows for that spot. When it returns nothing, the slotted menu is used; when there is neither, the
  browser shows its own menu.

`context.data` is what the clicked spot stands for. Before opening, the element dispatches the composed
`c2-context-menu-request` event on the node under the pointer, and a component that owns that node answers it
through `provideContextMenuData` from `@c2n/core/context-menu-helper.js`. `c2-table` answers with the cell
(`row`, `rowIndex`, `key`, `column`, `value`), so a table wrapped in a context menu gets per-cell menus with no
wiring. For plain markup, read `context.target` (`target.closest('[data-id]')`).

A nested `c2-context-menu` wins over the one around it, and so does any handler that already called
`preventDefault()` on the `contextmenu` event. Set `disabled` to let the browser's own menu through.

Style the surface through the `--c2-menu--*` variables, set on this element or anywhere above it.
declarations.name: ContextMenu

slots.description: The area that opens the menu.
slots.name: default

slots.description: A `c2-menu` shown when `renderContextMenu` is not set or returns nothing.
slots.name: menu

members.name: renderContextMenu
members.description:
Returns the rows for the spot that was clicked. Called on every opening; see ContextMenuRenderer. A property
only, since it holds a function.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Ignores right clicks and long presses, so the browser shows its own menu.

members.name: longPressDuration
members.description: How long, in milliseconds, a finger or pen must rest before the menu opens.

members.name: menuLabel
members.description: Accessible name of a menu built by `renderContextMenu`. A slotted menu takes its own `aria-label`.

members.name: dynamicContent
members.description: Rows returned by `renderContextMenu` for the current opening.

members.name: returnFocusTo
members.description: Where focus was before the menu took it, restored when the menu closes.

members.name: listenedMenus
members.description: Menus slotted into `menu` that carry our `toggle` listener.

type.text: { timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; pointerId: number; x: number; y: number } | undefined

members.name: suppressClick
members.description: A long press opened the menu, so the click the lifted finger produces must not reach the content.

members.name: lastOpen
members.description: When the last menu opened, and how: a native `contextmenu` for the same gesture right after is a duplicate.

members.name: presenting
members.description: An opening is under way; a `closed` toggle from the menu it is reopening is not the end of the menu.

members.name: generation
members.description: Incremented per opening, so a slower earlier opening never shows after a later one.

members.name: open
members.description: Whether the menu is showing.

members.name: context
members.description: The context of the menu that is showing, or of the last one shown.

members.name: staticMenu
members.description: The `c2-menu` slotted into `menu`, if any.

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the menu at viewport coordinates `x`, `y`. `target` is the element the context is about (this element by
default); it is also where the data request is dispatched. Returns whether a menu opened.

members.name: areaChild
members.description: The light-DOM child of this element an event came through, when it belongs to the area (not the menu).

members.name: fromMenu
members.description:
Whether the event came from one of the menus, which get no browser menu on top of them. A slotted child's path
runs through this element's slot and shadow root too, so the internal menu is tested for, not the shadow root.

members.name: handleClickCapture
members.description: The finger that long-pressed lifts with a click; it opened the menu and must not also activate the content.

members.name: placeAnchor
members.description:
Moves the zero-size anchor under the pointer. `position: fixed` resolves against a transformed ancestor instead of
the viewport, so measure where it landed and correct by the difference.

members.name: restoreFocus
members.description: The menu hands focus back to its anchor, which is a point, not a control: return it to where it was instead.

events.name: context-menu-open
events.description: Fired before the menu opens, with the context as `detail`. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the menu closed and lets the browser's menu show.
Fired when a row is activated: the row's `value`, `checked` and `data`, plus the `context` the menu was opened on. The row's own `menu-select` still bubbles as well.
events.name: context-menu-select

events.description: Fired after the menu opens or closes; `newState` is `open` or `closed`.
events.name: toggle

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Ignores right clicks and long presses, so the browser shows its own menu.

attributes.name: long-press-duration
attributes.description: How long, in milliseconds, a finger or pen must rest before the menu opens.

attributes.name: menu-label
attributes.description: Accessible name of a menu built by `renderContextMenu`. A slotted menu takes its own `aria-label`.
